issues.t: Throttle body failure causes limp mode or stalling
issues.sym: The check engine light or orange wrench light comes on and the car suddenly loses power and won't go much above idle speed. It may also stall or idle roughly.
issues.why: Dirt builds up on the electrical contacts inside the electronic throttle body motor, so the computer loses track of the throttle and cuts power to protect the engine. Ford extended throttle body coverage on affected vehicles of this era (program 13N03), and NHTSA lists many speed-control complaints for the 2005 Montego.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. If power drops, move to a safe spot and turn on your hazards. Restarting may restore power briefly, but get it to a shop soon. The extended coverage has expired by age, but ask a Ford dealer anyway.

issues.t: CVT slips, shudders or won't engage
issues.sym: On cars with the CVT (continuously variable transmission), the engine revs but the car slows, drops out of gear, or only 'shifts when it wants to'. Wrench and check engine lights often come on.
issues.why: The CVT used in the Montego and Ford Five Hundred wears internally (bearings and the valve body are cited), and replacing the unit is a major repair.
issues.next: If the car loses drive, get off the road. Have the codes read; a software reflash or valve body sometimes fixes it, but a failing CVT usually needs a used or remanufactured unit.

issues.t: Six-speed automatic shifts hard or fails
issues.sym: On cars with the six-speed automatic, harsh downshifts, clunks into gear, hesitation, or eventually slipping and loss of drive.
issues.why: Owners report software updates, valve body replacement and, in some cases, a rebuilt transmission to fix shifting faults in the six-speed.
issues.next: Ask a Ford dealer to check for transmission software updates first. If it slips, avoid hard driving and get it diagnosed before the damage spreads.

issues.sym: The car loses traction in snow or rain, or you hear grinding, whining or clunking from underneath on AWD models.
issues.why: The AWD system's rear drive unit and transfer unit can fail. Owners report major repairs.
issues.next: Have the AWD unit's fluid and operation checked. Keep tires matched in size and wear, since mismatched tires strain the AWD system.

issues.sym: The A/C blows warm or only cools while driving, or makes a grinding noise.
issues.why: The A/C compressor is the most common repair reported on the Montego's twin, the Ford Five Hundred.
issues.next: Have the system pressures and compressor clutch checked. A failed compressor usually needs a new drier and expansion valve too.

issues.sym: A clunk when shifting into drive or reverse, extra vibration at idle, or the engine rocking when you accelerate.
issues.why: The engine mounts crack or collapse, sometimes at low mileage.
issues.next: Have the mounts checked while someone shifts between drive and reverse with the brake on. Replace broken mounts soon to protect hoses and the exhaust.

issues.sym: The battery keeps going dead, the battery light comes on, or lights dim.
issues.why: Alternator failures are common on these cars, and owners also report batteries that won't hold a charge.
issues.next: Have the battery and charging system tested together before replacing parts.

issues.t: EGR valve failure turns on the check engine light
issues.sym: A check engine light, sometimes with rough idle or hesitation.
issues.why: The exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) valve fails on these engines; some cars need it more than once.
issues.next: Have the codes read. An EGR fault is not urgent, but fix it to pass emissions and keep the engine running smoothly.

issues.sym: A burning oil smell, oil on the outside of the engine, or smoke from the engine bay.
issues.why: The valve cover gaskets harden and leak oil onto the exhaust.
issues.next: Check your oil level. Replace the gaskets before oil soaks the spark plug wells or drips on hot parts.

issues.sym: Grinding, a burning smell from one wheel, the car pulling to one side, or one set of pads wearing much faster.
issues.why: Calipers, especially at the rear, seize on these cars.
issues.next: Have the brakes inspected. Replace a sticking caliper with pads and rotors on that axle.

issues.t: Front end creaks or clunks over bumps
issues.sym: Clunks, creaks or rattles from the front over bumps or when turning.
issues.why: Worn sway bar end links, tie rod ends, control arm bushings and strut mounts are frequent repairs.
issues.next: Have the front suspension inspected. Worn tie rods affect steering, so replace them promptly and get an alignment.

issues.t: Power steering pump leaks or whines
issues.sym: Whining when turning, fluid under the front, or heavier steering.
issues.why: The power steering pump develops leaks on these cars.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and look for leaks. Replace the pump if it leaks or groans.

issues.sym: A bouncy or floaty ride, knocking over bumps, or a clunk when turning the wheel at low speed.
issues.why: Front and rear struts and the strut mounts and bearings wear out on these cars, often past 90,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the struts checked for leaks and the mounts for play. Replace struts in pairs and get an alignment afterward.

issues.sym: A humming or growling noise that gets louder with speed.
issues.why: Wheel bearings and hubs wear out on these cars.
issues.next: Have the bearings checked for play. Replace a noisy bearing before it gets loose.

issues.sym: Dash gauges or cluster lights flicker, go dark or stop working.
issues.why: The instrument cluster can fail internally and needs repair or replacement.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: you may not see your speed or warning lights, so ease off, keep a safe distance, and pull over where it's safe. Restarting the car once parked may bring the display back; if it doesn't, have it fixed before you drive again. Have the cluster tested. A rebuilt cluster is usually an option instead of a new one.

issues.sym: The driver's heated seat stops warming.
issues.why: The seat heater element fails; one owner of the twin Ford Five Hundred replaced it three times.
issues.next: Not a safety issue. Check the fuse and switch first, then the element.

issues.sym: A ticking noise, especially on a cold start, or an exhaust smell.
issues.why: The exhaust manifold can crack with age and heat.
issues.next: Have the leak confirmed. Fix it soon, since exhaust leaks can let fumes into the cabin and upset oxygen sensor readings.

issues.t: Paint bubbling and peeling on the hood
issues.sym: Small bubbles along the front edge of the hood that spread and peel.
issues.why: The aluminum hood's paint lifts; body shops blame poor prep or oxidation of the aluminum.
issues.next: This is cosmetic. Repainting may not last, so many owners replace the hood instead.

issues.sym: A door may not stay latched or may open while moving.
issues.why: Under recall 06V-383, the door latch pawl may not return to the latched position, so a door could open while driving.
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls and have the latches replaced free at a Ford dealer. Always confirm doors are fully shut.

issues.sym: A rattle or clunk from under the rear, or a fuel smell or leak.
issues.why: Under recall 05V-515, a fuel tank strap could break, causing noise or a fuel leak with a fire risk.
issues.next: If you smell fuel, don't drive the car. Check your VIN for this recall.
